titleStmt.title: Memorandum From Secretary of State Haig to President Reagan

div.head: Memorandum From Secretary of State Haig to President Reagan
div.p: Venezuelan President Herrera’s letter to you regretting that he cannot visit in April gives a frank presentation of Venezuelan views on hemispheric affairs. Venezuela pursues foreign policy goals in the hemisphere which largely coincide with ours, including strong support for the Duarte government in El Salvador. Still, we believe an important reason for Herrera’s decision not to accept your invitation at this time was concern about having to situate himself in public vis-a-vis U. S. policies in Central America and the Caribbean.

Venezuela recognizes its profound self-interest in countering Cuba in the Caribbean area and actively opposes Cuban destabilization. U.S. and Venezuelan interests coincide in this respect. It is in our interest to encourage, influence and work with Venezuelan activism in the region. However, in his letter Herrera also repeats the idea he has been developing publicly that Latin America must be a “zone of peace without foreign interference.” That is simply not realistic, and we should tell him so, courteously and warmly.
I recommend that you send the attached reply to Herrera. Meanwhile, we should hold up notification of our decision to sell Venezuela F–16A’s (desirable in itself) until your exchange is complete.

note.p: Attached as Attachment 2 but not printed are Herrera’s March 27 letter to Reagan and a translation.

In an undated note to Allen, Colson wrote: “RVA: I think (and Fontaine concurs) that Haig’s memo contains another effort to end-run the White House on the sale of F–16s to Venezuela. As you know, we have told State that such a sale will not proceed until there has been a comprehensive Presidential review of arms transfers/sales in general. Haig seems to ignore this in paragraph #3 of his memo to the President, when he states that ‘meanwhile we should hold up notification of our decision to sell Venezuela F–16A’s (desirable in itself) until your exchange is complete.’ Have we/has the President decided to sell the Venezuelans the F–16??? Janet.” (Reagan Library, Executive Secretariat, NSC Head of State File, Venezuela: President Herrera (8100642–8202071))
